turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on back and hop up on the table. I'll pull that dressing off and grab vitals while he's wrestling with the computer.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. It pulls when I climb up. I don't know, it's just sore.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Temp is 38.2 Celsius, pulse 96, blood pressure 146 over 88, oxygen 97 percent, respirations 18.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Dressing's off. Right groin incision, the middle is split open a little, redness about two inches all around, and there's yellow-green drainage on the gauze.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I come by in the mornings, she lives alone, and today the bandage was soaked through. It wasn't like that on Monday.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this screen keeps flipping back to the last chart. What was that blood pressure again?
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): 146 over 88. Temp's still 38.2.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): All right. What brings you in?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): The cut from the hernia surgery. It's red and there's gunk coming out, and last night I had a fever. I was shaking under the blanket.
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was burning up around midnight. At breakfast she said she felt a little better, but she's still warm.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hernia repair, right? How long ago was that?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten days. Right groin. I don't know, doctor, the exact date — it was a Tuesday.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did the drainage start?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): The neighbor's dog barked all night, I couldn't sleep, and my back is sore from the couch.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): The inbox just popped up. Say again, when did the drainage start?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, um, two days ago? I don't know, doctor. Maybe Tuesday, I really don't know.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Did the redness start around then too?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, around then. It hurts if I walk.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any red streaks up the belly or down the thigh?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just right around the cut.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting or diarrhea?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting. And no diarrhea.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): What about nausea?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll leave that. Any shortness of breath or chest pain?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Which antibiotic did they send you home with?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): The white capsules. Keflex, I think, and I thought they were 250 milligrams. I took them five days... or was it seven? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0029] person_1 (NURSE): The discharge summary says cephalexin, 500 milligrams by mouth, four times a day, for seven days.
[SEG0030] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The pharmacy bottle said 500 milligrams. She won't wear her glasses.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hold on, the screen jumped. What dose was on the bottle?
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): 500 milligrams. She still thinks it was 250.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Did you take it four times a day, the whole way through?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I might have missed some. The days all ran together.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Anything else you take every day?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): The water tablet in the morning, for my high blood pressure. And Tylenol, two tablets, when the cut really hurts.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right, for the blood pressure. That water tablet — what's the name on it? What strength?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Little white pill, once a day. That's all I know.
[SEG0039] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I looked at the bottle at the house. I still can't tell you the name.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergies?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Sulfa. I get a rash all over. That one I know.

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): No sulfa drugs, then. Let me look. Yeah, erythema and purulent drainage right on the groin incision. I'm calling this a surgical site infection for now, till the culture comes back.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): Swab kit's right here if you want it.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yeah, swab the wound and send it for culture. We're stopping the Keflex. I'll start Augmentin, 875 milligrams by mouth twice a day for seven days.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take it with food. Keep a dry gauze on it, and wash your hands before you change the dressing.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a day. I don't know, doctor, I'll try to remember.

[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the redness spreads, the fever climbs, or you can't keep the pills down, come back sooner. Otherwise I'll see you in three days, and the front desk can book it once this computer lets me sign.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
